purpose: F-01 next-work item from VERIFIER_NEXT_EVIDENCE.md: 'identify the actual host CPU hotspots' behind the 400M-metered-instruction Soroban verification exhaustion. Uses the pinned Binius64 verifier's own pre-existing tracing::info_span! instrumentation (unmodified upstream source) to attribute native, single-threaded, release-build wall-clock cost across verification layers. This is a relative-cost-distribution proxy, not a Soroban metered-instruction count, and is not a security review.
method: A new, isolated tool directory (tools/binius-verifier-profile-research/) builds a native binary over the exact pinned fixtures already used throughout this project's Binius64 evidence, reusing the existing frozen.rs loader via #[path] (no duplication). It installs a hand-rolled tracing::Subscriber (no new dependency beyond the already-locked tracing v0.1.44 crate) that times every info_span! enter/exit already present in the pinned, unmodified upstream source, keyed by (span name, nesting depth, occurrence ordinal) -- the ordinal is necessary because two call sites share the span name 'Verify' at the same nesting depth (0) as sequential siblings, not nested, which a plain name+depth key would otherwise conflate.

architectural_finding.summary: The two 'Verify' spans are NOT parent/child as a first read of the source's lexical/RAII structure might suggest. Confirmed directly against crates/verifier/src/zk_config.rs:153-170 (ZKVerifier::verify): they are two sequential top-level calls.

layer_a.description: The inner structural-IOP verify (IntMul/BitAnd/Shift/PublicInput reduction + a 'PCS Opening' phase), run through ZKWrappedVerifierChannel, which per the module's own doc comment RECORDS values as outer public inputs rather than performing the real BaseFold cryptographic check. The 5 [phase] sub-spans measured inside this layer are this recording/bookkeeping pass, not the real verification cost, despite one of them being literally named 'PCS Opening'.

layer_b.description: Runs the real outer Spartan verification: verify_mulcheck (masked zerocheck for A*B=C, crates/spartan-verifier/src/lib.rs) plus the actual channel.verify_oracle_relations BaseFold/FRI opening (Merkle-path + field-arithmetic checks), batched over ALL inner+outer oracles together. No further tracing::info_span! instrumentation exists upstream inside this call, so this tool cannot decompose it further without adding new spans, which would mean patching pinned/frozen source -- not done here, consistent with this project's standing discipline against modifying pinned dependencies.

architectural_finding.conclusion: The dominant verification cost is NOT the structural IOP's IntMul/BitAnd/Shift bit-operation reductions, and is NOT located inside the span literally named '[phase] Verify PCS Opening' (that span fires during the cheap recording pass, layer A). The real, expensive BaseFold/FRI polynomial-commitment opening together with the Spartan mulcheck both run inside the single unlabeled layer-B span, which this instrumentation cannot further subdivide without new spans in pinned source. Any F-01 optimization effort should target layer B specifically -- most plausibly the BaseFold opening's Merkle-path verification and field arithmetic over the batched oracle set -- rather than the bit-operation reduction phases layer A's [phase] spans name.
architectural_finding.correction_note: An earlier reading of this project's own source review (naming the two layers 'Phase 1: mulcheck' then 'Phase 2: PCS opening', in that call order) had the call order backwards and under-specified layer B's content. This file supersedes that framing with the call order and content confirmed directly against zk_config.rs.

scope_and_limits: Native, single-threaded, release-build wall-clock timing, not a Soroban metered-instruction count; the relative cost DISTRIBUTION across layers is the result, not an absolute Soroban cost prediction.
Confirms the existing canonical fixture is accepted (verifier_accepted: true) in every run; this tool performs no new cryptographic claim and changes no account, asset, or authorization state.
Does not itself reduce SDK code size, reduce metered instructions, or close F-01; it narrows WHERE a reduction effort should focus.
Does not decompose layer B further; doing so would require adding new tracing spans inside pinned upstream source, which this project avoids modifying.
